description:
# DemoApp.CollaborativeEditor Issues 2

The `DemoApp.CollaborativeEditor` still crashes while typing and other clients sync but not often as in previous run named 'demoapp-collaborativeeditor-issues-the-collab' (research about it in `.wig/runs/demoapp-collaborativeeditor-issues-the-collab`). 

I reviewed the code and I see that we completely ignored the fact that request was to **mandatory use Automerge's** **repo pattern** and that we are doing manual document editing, saving, etc. 

Research id depth about Repo here:
- [Automerge Repo: A "batteries-included" toolkit for building local-first applications](https://automerge.org/blog/automerge-repo/)
- [automerge/automerge-repo](https://github.com/automerge/automerge-repo)

Also research in the provided source code in `.references/automerge-repo-2.5.3/` how it works and how it should be used.

Also, it seems `DemoApp.CollaborativeEditor` is first version of the demo app and we also have the `DemoApp.CollaborativeTextEditor` that is the second version and it uses repo pattern in some way but it seems not correct as it also directly modifies the document and have same crashing issues also.

## What to do

- Delete the `DemoApp.CollaborativeTextEditor` project as it is duplicate
- **MANDATORY: Use the Autmerge Repo** **. Do NOT edit Document manually!**
- **MANDATORY: Stop using sync methods and force async methods converted to sync (configure async, wait etc..** This is highly async library and it should work that way out of the box.
- As I mentioned, `DemoApp.CollaborativeEditor` still crashes when typing. The fishy thing is that when some client crash, all other clients stop responding so something happens on the server too. We need to research and investigate this.
- You are doing document editing and some weird manipulations directly in `EditorViewModel`. Text editing should work out of the box, not specific to some application. For example in `ApplyTextChange` .. this is a shit storm! If we need to have specific implementation to make Automerge work with text documents, better make a new library that would provide out-of-the box solution for text editing capabilities with Automerge. Same way with Figma like drawing/editing in `DemoApp.CollaborativeDrawing`.
- I think we need to use some kind of debouncing/throttling of updates to avoid hogging the network and server. I think I saw that Repo or NetworkAdapter has that built in. If not, built that into C# implementation of Repo.
- Marks do not work (bold, italics, etc.) They are not set neither on the client that sets the text, nor propagated to the clients that are recieving changes. Make marks work.
- The info in top righ corner is always 'Resuming document...'. It seems that we are not updating editor status correctly.
- Start the apps using `Infra.AppHost`. This starts Aspire app hosts and all needed apps will be started automatically
- Use `six.avalonia.mcp` to write text in a way I described to see what is happening and when some of other clients will crash.
- Create new document in one client and then connect with other clients using document id
- Observe logs and traces whole time to know what is happening during the whole time

## CRITICAL
- USE ASPIRE!!! Start `Infra.AppHost` and then use user interface to write and observe
qaHistory:
Let me thoroughly explore the codebase first to understand the current state before asking questions.Now let me also check some specific details I still need.Now let me check the sync layer to understand how sync messages are throttled/not-throttled.I've now thoroughly explored the codebase. Here are my clarifying questions:

**Q1 — Library naming and scope for text editing**
You mentioned extracting text editing into a reusable library. I see the current `AutomergeService` in `DemoApp.CollaborativeEditor/Services/` does text splicing, marks, cursors, spans, and blocks. What should the new library be called? I'm thinking `Six.Automerge.Text` — a standalone library that provides:
- Text document abstraction wrapping `DocHandle<T>` (not raw `AutomergeDocument`)
- Diff/splice algorithm (the `ApplyTextChange` logic, cleaned up)
- Cursor management (save/restore across edits)
- Mark operations (bold/italic/underline/link)
- Change batching/debouncing for rapid typing

Does this scope sound right, or do you want it narrower/broader?

**Q2 — Rich text rendering**
Marks (bold/italic/underline) are being stored in the Automerge CRDT via `doc.Mark()`, but the UI uses a plain Avalonia `TextBox` which **cannot render rich text**. Making marks "work" has two meanings:
- (a) Marks persist in the CRDT and propagate to other peers (data layer)
- (b) Marks are visually rendered in the editor (UI layer)

For (b), we'd need to replace `TextBox` with a rich text control (e.g., AvaloniaEdit or a custom FlowDocument-style renderer). Do you want both (a) and (b), or just (a) for now?

**Q3 — Sync message throttling**
Currently, every single keystroke triggers an immediate sync message to ALL peers (no throttling). The TypeScript reference implementation throttles sync at 100ms. Should I add sync throttling at the `DocSynchronizer` level (matching the TS pattern), or at a different layer? The save debounce already exists at 100ms in Repo.

**Q4 — Server role**
Currently the `Server.Api` acts purely as a SignalR relay — documents sync peer-to-peer through it but aren't stored server-side (the Orleans `DocumentGrain` is a scaffold with no real logic). Should the server remain a pure relay, or should we implement server-side document persistence in the Orleans grain?

**Q5 — DemoApp.CollaborativeTextEditor**
You said to delete this duplicate project. I confirmed it exists with its own `TextEditorViewModel`, `AutomergeService`, etc. I'll delete the entire `apps/DemoApp.CollaborativeTextEditor/` directory and remove any references from `Infra.AppHost`. Should I also delete the test project `tests/DemoApp.CollaborativeTextEditor.Tests/` that goes with it?

**Q6 — Existing tests**
The `DemoApp.CollaborativeEditor.Tests` project has 67 tests, many of which test the current direct-document-manipulation pattern. Since we're refactoring to go through `DocHandle.ChangeAsync()` exclusively and extracting a library, should I rewrite these tests for the new architecture, or try to adapt the existing ones?

**Q7 — Number of editor replicas**
The AppHost currently starts **4 replicas** of `CollaborativeEditor`. Is 4 the right number for testing, or should it be different (e.g., 2 or 3)?

**Q8 — Crash investigation approach**
You mention "when some client crashes, all other clients stop responding." This suggests the server-side hub might be failing or the sync protocol corrupts state for all peers. Should investigating and fixing this crash be a top priority (Sprint 1), or should we first refactor to the proper Repo pattern (which may eliminate the crashes as a side effect)?

Q1 - That's ok, do it. Name the library Six.Automerge.TextEdit Q2 - I meant B. You can set marks in Avalonia using spans like (XAML example, but you can do it in the code also): This is a TextBlock with several Span elements, using a variety of styles . Q3 - Add it then to DocSynchronizer but Six.Automerge.TextEdit should have a way to configure it higher level Q4 - We are not using Orleans anymore in this project. In this example, server should store it's own document version but it should be saved also with some debounding or with timers (not after each change since it would hog the server with huge documents). I would also like to make a separate library named Six.Automerge.SyncServer that is a plug and play library for client-server usecases of Automerge where the server holds the TRUTH and relays the messages. Keep the implementation flexible so we can use it later with Orleans (that will be another project and set of libraries) Q5 - Yes Q6 - Yes, rewrite Q7 - Set as you seems fit for the testing. I tought that 4 is ok so test a bit more load Q8 - First refactor so we have a state of the repo we want, then we will deeply test and fix all issues

I now have comprehensive understanding of the entire codebase. Let me write the three spec files.All three spec files have been written:

1. **requirements.md** — 8 functional requirements (Repo pattern, TextEdit library, SyncServer library, rich text rendering, fully async, sync throttling, editor status, cleanup) and 4 non-functional requirements (stability, performance, testability, architecture)

2. **design.md** — Full architecture with:
   - `Six.Automerge.TextEdit` library: `TextDocument`, `TextDiff`, `ChangeDebouncer`, `FormattedText` model, `CursorTracker`

   - Sync throttling via deferred-final pattern in `DocSynchronizer`
   - Rich text rendering using Avalonia Spans (dual-layer: TextBox for input, TextBlock for display)
   - Complete data flow diagrams

3. **implementation-plan.md** — 9 sprints:
   - Sprint 1: Cleanup & sync throttling (7 tasks)
   - Sprint 2: TextEdit core (8 tasks)
   - Sprint 3: TextEdit factories & tests (8 tasks)
   - Sprint 4: SyncServer library (8 tasks)
   - Sprint 5: Refactor Server.Api (6 tasks)
   - Sprint 6: Refactor EditorViewModel (7 tasks)
   - Sprint 7: Rich text rendering (6 tasks)

   - Sprint 9: Integration testing with Aspire (8 tasks)
